title: Handwriting in the Digital Age
context: 數位時代還要學寫字嗎
instructions: You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: In 2016, schools in Finland stopped being required to teach joined-up handwriting, the flowing style in which the letters of each word are connected. Lessons in typing were to take its place. The decision attracted attention around the world, partly because Finland's education system is so widely admired, and it prompted a question that many parents and teachers had already begun to ask: in an age when most writing is done on a keyboard or a touchscreen, is there any point in teaching children to form letters with a pen?

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Until recently, the debate was conducted mainly in terms of tradition and convenience. Defenders of handwriting spoke of personal expression and of the pleasure of a well-written letter; its critics replied that such arguments were merely nostalgic, and that classroom time would be better spent on skills that employers actually want. Over the past two decades, however, psychologists and neuroscientists have begun to gather evidence, and their findings suggest that the way we write may affect how well we learn.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Some of the most striking results concern young children. Karin James, a psychologist at Indiana University, worked with children who had not yet learned to read. Each child was shown a letter and asked to reproduce it in one of three ways: by drawing it freehand on blank paper, by tracing over a dotted outline, or by typing it on a keyboard. The children were then shown the letters again while their brains were scanned. In those who had drawn the letters freehand, there was activity in areas of the brain that adults use for reading. In the other two groups, the response was much weaker. James suggests that the very messiness of a child's handwriting is useful: because no two attempts at a letter are alike, the child learns what all versions of that letter have in common.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Handwriting may also influence what older children compose. Virginia Berninger, of the University of Washington, followed pupils between the ages of seven and twelve and compared the essays they produced with a pen and with a keyboard. When writing by hand, the children wrote more words, wrote them faster and expressed more ideas. Berninger does not conclude that keyboards should be kept out of classrooms. Her argument is rather that the two methods are not interchangeable, and that children should be taught both.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: For students, the question usually arises in the lecture hall. In a widely reported study published in 2014, Pam Mueller and Daniel Oppenheimer asked university students to watch recorded talks and take notes, either on a laptop or in a notebook. The two groups remembered facts equally well, but those who had used laptops performed worse on questions that required them to understand and apply ideas. The explanation appeared to lie in the notes themselves. The laptop users, who could type quickly, tended to record the speaker's words more or less exactly. Those writing by hand could not keep up, so they were forced to select and summarise – in other words, to think about what they were hearing. Even when laptop users were specifically told not to copy word for word, they found it hard to stop.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Brain recordings point in a similar direction. At the Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Audrey van der Meer fitted students with caps containing more than 250 sensors and measured the electrical activity in their brains as they wrote words by hand or typed them. Handwriting produced far more widespread patterns of activity, particularly in regions associated with memory. Van der Meer attributes this to the complex and varied movements involved in shaping each letter, in contrast to the identical tap of a finger that produces every letter on a keyboard.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: It would be a mistake, however, to treat the case as closed. Several of these studies involved small numbers of participants, and when other researchers repeated the note-taking experiment in 2019, the advantage of handwriting was smaller than originally reported and not always statistically reliable. Nor does anyone seriously dispute the practical advantages of typing: typed text is easier to edit, to share and to read, and for children with certain physical or learning difficulties a keyboard removes a real barrier. The most sensible conclusion may be the one that Berninger reached. Handwriting deserves its place in school not because it is traditional but because it appears to do something that typing does not – and the same could be said in reverse.

groups.instruction:
Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A–G.
Which paragraph contains the following information?
groups.limit:
Write the correct letter, A–G, next to Questions 14–18.
NB You may use any letter more than once.

items.text: a reference to doubts about how strong some of the research evidence is
a description of the terms in which handwriting used to be discussed
an explanation of why writing slowly can be an advantage
an example of a change in one country's educational requirements
a mention of learners for whom typing is especially helpful

groups.instruction:
Look at the following findings or claims (Questions 19–22) and the list of researchers below.
Match each finding or claim with the correct researcher(s), A, B, C or D.
groups.limit: Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, next to Questions 19–22.

items.text: The irregular shapes of handwritten letters help learners to identify the essential features of each letter.
The physical movements made in handwriting are more varied than those made in typing.
Pupils ought to learn to write both by hand and on a keyboard.
Asking people to change the way they took notes had little effect.

groups.limit: Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

questions.explain:
答案是 G。G 段指出好幾個研究的受試者人數少（small numbers of participants），而且 2019 年重做記筆記實驗時，手寫的優勢比原本報告的小，也不一定在統計上可靠。
同義轉換：not always statistically reliable ＝ doubts about how strong the evidence is。
questions.quote: the advantage of handwriting was smaller than originally reported and not always statistically reliable

questions.explain:
答案是 B。B 段說這場辯論過去主要是 in terms of tradition and convenience，支持者談個人風格，反對者說那只是懷舊。
同義轉換：Until recently... was conducted in terms of ＝ the terms in which... used to be discussed。
questions.quote: Until recently, the debate was conducted mainly in terms of tradition and convenience.

questions.explain:
答案是 E。E 段解釋手寫的人 could not keep up（跟不上），所以被迫篩選和摘要，也就是必須思考聽到的內容。
解題關鍵：題目的 writing slowly 在原文沒有直接出現，要從 could not keep up 理解成「寫得慢」，而這反而變成優點。
questions.quote: Those writing by hand could not keep up, so they were forced to select and summarise

questions.explain:
答案是 A。A 段開頭就是 Finland 的例子：2016 年起學校不再被要求教連筆字，改上打字課。
同義轉換：stopped being required to teach ＝ a change in educational requirements；Finland ＝ one country。
questions.quote: In 2016, schools in Finland stopped being required to teach joined-up handwriting

questions.explain:
答案是 G。G 段提到對於有某些肢體或學習困難的孩子，a keyboard removes a real barrier。
解題關鍵：這題和第 14 題答案相同，指示中的 NB 已經提醒同一個字母可以用不只一次。
questions.quote: for children with certain physical or learning difficulties a keyboard removes a real barrier

questions.explain:
答案是 A（Karin James）。她認為孩子字跡的 messiness（凌亂）有用：每次寫出來都不一樣，孩子因此學到同一個字母所有寫法的共同點。
同義轉換：messiness / no two attempts are alike ＝ irregular shapes；what all versions have in common ＝ essential features。
questions.quote: because no two attempts at a letter are alike, the child learns what all versions of that letter have in common

questions.explain:
答案是 D（Audrey van der Meer）。她把腦部活動的差異歸因於寫每個字母時 complex and varied movements，相對於鍵盤上每個字母都是同樣的敲擊。
同義轉換：identical tap of a finger 對比 varied movements ＝ more varied than typing。
questions.quote: Van der Meer attributes this to the complex and varied movements involved in shaping each letter

questions.explain:
答案是 C（Virginia Berninger）。她不認為鍵盤該被趕出教室，而是主張兩種方式不能互相取代，children should be taught both。
陷阱：G 段結尾也贊同這個結論，但明說那是 the one that Berninger reached。
questions.quote: the two methods are not interchangeable, and that children should be taught both

questions.explain:
答案是 B（Mueller and Oppenheimer）。在他們的研究中，即使特別告訴用筆電的學生不要逐字抄，they found it hard to stop。
同義轉換：specifically told not to ＝ asking people to change；found it hard to stop ＝ had little effect。
questions.quote: Even when laptop users were specifically told not to copy word for word, they found it hard to stop.

questions.explain:
答案是 notebook。學生看錄影演講並記筆記，either on a laptop or in a notebook。
解題關鍵：空格前的 in a 與原文完全相同，直接對應。
questions.quote: take notes, either on a laptop or in a notebook

questions.explain:
答案是 facts。原文 The two groups remembered facts equally well。
同義轉換：remembered... equally well ＝ equally good at remembering。
questions.quote: The two groups remembered facts equally well

questions.explain:
答案是 ideas。用筆電的學生在需要 understand and apply ideas 的題目上表現較差。
陷阱：不要填 questions。題目的動詞是 understand and apply，受詞是 ideas。
questions.quote: performed worse on questions that required them to understand and apply ideas

questions.explain:
答案是 summarise（摘要）。手寫的人跟不上，so they were forced to select and summarise。
解題關鍵：空格前是 select and，要填另一個原形動詞。美式拼法 summarize 也算對。
questions.quote: so they were forced to select and summarise
